proposed_bechina_edges.proof_text: הַמְכַסֶּה שָׁמַיִם בְּעָבִים – הַיְנוּ אֵשׁ וּמַיִם. הַיְנוּ כְּשֶׁהַצַּדִּיק יָכוֹל לְכַסּוֹת שָׁמַיִם, הַיְנוּ אֵשׁ וּמַיִם, הַיְנוּ הָאַהֲבָה וְהַיִּרְאָה שֶׁלּוֹ
הַמְכַסֶּה שָׁמַיִם בְּעָבִים – הַיְנוּ אֵשׁ וּמַיִם
כִּי הַצַּדִּיק יֵשׁ לוֹ יָדַיִם בַּמֶּה לְקַבְּלָם, דְּהַיְנוּ אַהֲבָה וְיִרְאָה, כִּי הֵם הַיָּדַיִם לְקַבֵּל בָּהֶם כָּל הַהַשְׁפָּעוֹת
לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם, הַיְנוּ לְשֵׁם צַדִּיק, שֶׁהוּא מְכֻנֶּה בְּשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם, מֵחֲמַת שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ אַהֲבָה וְיִרְאָה
הַמְכַסֶּה שָׁמַיִם בְּעָבִים... וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא נוֹתֵן בְּלֵב צַדִּיק אַחֵר לְהַחַזִיק עָלָיו בְּמַחֲלֹקֶת כְּדֵי לְכַסּוֹתוֹ
proposed_bechina_edges.confidence: medium — the equation is structural/interpretive (the verse's clouds = the teaching's controversy) rather than explicitly stated with בחינת or הינו language

new_packages.reason: Torah #88 is built on the equation: the heavens (שמים) = fire + water (אש ומים) = love + fear (אהבה ויראה). The tzaddik is called by the name 'heavens' precisely because he possesses this love and fear. Love and fear ARE his 'hands' (ידים) — his receptive instruments for drawing divine influx downward. The clouds (עבים) that 'cover the heavens' in the verse are equated with the controversy (מחלוקת) that conceals the tzaddik. All of these concepts share the same essential nature: they are aspects of the tzaddik's concealed holy identity — the hidden inner fire-and-water that makes him capable of drawing divine blessing. This cluster is unambiguously 'good' (holy) because: (1) love and fear of God are the highest spiritual virtues, (2) the tzaddik's identity as 'heavens' is a title of supreme holiness, and (3) even the controversy (מחלוקת) in this teaching is 'for the sake of heaven' — a divinely-ordained protective act, not a negative force.
new_packages.relationship_to_existing_packages: This proposed package is the cause (eitza) of the existing Package 1 (מטר/השפעות וברכות): the tzaddik's concealed love/fear [NEW-1] → enables rain/influx [Package 1] to flow to the world. The two packages are connected by eitza, not bechina. They represent two distinct conceptual domains: the tzaddik's inner spiritual state (NEW-1) vs. the divine blessing that flows as a result (Package 1).
new_packages.good_evil_mirror: The evil mirror of this package would be a cluster around the מקטרגים (accusers) who observe and block the tzaddik. However, no bechina language equates מקטרגים with any other concept in Torah #88 — the evil side is present functionally (via eitza) but not as a bechina cluster. The evil mirror is structurally implicit (famous tzaddik → exposed to מקטרגים → they block the influx) but cannot be formalized as a bechina package without additional source text equating the מקטרגים with a named evil concept.

observations: Torah #88 requires one new package: the cluster of concepts centered on the tzaddik's concealed love and fear. This is not a new conceptual type in the Likutay Moharan vocabulary — love, fear, and the tzaddik appear across many Torahs — but within Torah #88, their specific identification with שמים (heavens), ידים (hands), and the mechanism of concealment forms a tightly-bounded bechina domain that deserves its own package. The teaching has a clean two-package structure once all bechinas are captured: (1) the tzaddik's inner holy fire-and-water [love/fear/hands/heavens/controversy] and (2) the divine rain/influx that flows as a result. These two packages are connected by the eitza: the tzaddik conceals his love-and-fear (Package NEW-1) in order to draw down the rain/influx (Package 1). The current dataset captures only Package 1 (partially) and an anomalous edge for Package 2 (שכינה/אלהים), missing the entire conceptual core of the teaching. Recommendation: add 4-5 new bechina edges for reference 88 to properly represent this Torah in the dataset.
